3 pressure valves

Pond Line
Bathhouse Line
Grove Line

the inner maintenance alcove
the way to the clue
the party gear reward
Why it works

This fits the father’s theme really well:

mason
mechanical tinkerer
estate builder
protective, overengineered household systems

Eight types of psychological horror worth exploring

1. The Almost Human — Uncanny Valley

Something looks almost perfectly human, except for one characteristic that is fundamentally wrong.

A person who never blinks. A face that remains expressionless while speaking. A smile that appears several seconds too late.

Inspiration: The Grudge, Invasion of the Body Snatchers.

2. Impossible Spaces — Spatial Dread

A familiar environment begins behaving impossibly.

Someone walks down a hallway and arrives at the room they just left. A door opens onto a wall that wasn't there before. A staircase seems to have one additional floor.

Inspiration: P.T., House.

3. The Unseen Presence — Being Watched

The players become convinced something is nearby without ever getting a clear look at it.

A chair moves in an empty room. Footsteps stop when someone turns around. A door slowly closes when nobody is near it.

Inspiration: The Blair Witch Project, Paranormal Activity.

4. Familiar Voices in Impossible Places

A familiar voice comes from somewhere it cannot possibly originate.

Someone hears themselves calling from the basement while standing upstairs. A deceased person calmly speaks from behind a locked door. A voice repeats something the party said privately.

Inspiration: The Evil Dead, SOMA.

5. Objects That Behave Almost Normally

An inanimate object behaves as though it possesses awareness.

A rocking horse stops rocking when watched. A painted portrait subtly changes expression. A toy is found facing the doorway every time the party reenters a room.

Inspiration: Poltergeist, The Conjuring.

6. Predatory Stillness

A creature stands perfectly motionless, watching. It never visibly approaches, but whenever attention shifts, it is closer.

The tension comes from the expectation that it will move, coupled with the inability to predict when.

Inspiration: Weeping Angels, It Follows.

7. Reflections and Identity Distortion

Someone's reflection moves a fraction of a second late. Their reflection remains standing after they leave the mirror. A figure reflected in a window isn't present in the room.

Inspiration: Oculus, Mirrors.

8. Anticipation Without Release

Players repeatedly experience indications that something terrible is about to happen, but nothing does.

Scratching comes from inside a wall. Breathing grows louder behind a closed door. Something heavy moves across the attic floor.

Then everything goes quiet.

Sound can be particularly effective in this style of horror. Experimental and game-design research suggests that unsettling audio can elevate tension even when there is no visible enemy.
